paper_metadata.title: QuanFraud: Quantum State Veriﬁcation Scheme for Fraud Detection in IoT-Assisted Quantum-Blockchain Networks

summary: The paper presents a gate-based hybrid fraud-detection pipeline using a 4-qubit QSVC/VQC circuit with ZZ-Feature-Map, Ry/Rz/CX ansatz, PCA/SMOTE preprocessing, and nested 10-fold validation on 20,468 records with 117 features. Reported performance is modest: QSVC achieves 0.4157 balanced accuracy, 0.625 recall, and 0.6524 F1, while classical Random Forest and XGBoost exceed 77% balanced accuracy; the paper also includes a separate 4-qubit GHZ-θ verification primitive with a 0.5 fidelity threshold.

experiments.description: Gate-based hybrid fraud-detection experiment using GHZ-θ state verification plus QSVC/VQC on a real financial fraud dataset with PCA/SMOTE preprocessing and 10-fold nested validation.

algorithm.variant: QSVC with ZZ-Feature-Map and trainable ansatz; VQC used as a hybrid comparator/optimizer
algorithm.ansatz: ZZFeatureMap followed by parameterized Ry/Rz/CX layers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are reduced with PCA and then encoded into a 4-qubit ZZ-Feature-Map / variational circuit; the paper also mentions amplitude encoding and angle re-uploading as ablation/alternative encodings, but the main reported pipeline uses ZZ-Feature-Map with PCA-reduced features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary fraud/anomaly classification on financial transaction data; QSVC/VQC outputs a fraud score Si and labels data as fraud if Si >= 0.75.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: GHZ-θ verification filters out disturbed samples before classification; SMOTE balances classes; threshold tuning and calibration are used for decision making.

problem_instance.description: Fraud detection on an IoT-assisted financial transaction dataset with identity metadata from DID/AnonCreds; quantum state verification is used to ensure channel integrity before scoring.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Kaggle fraud-detection bank dataset (Volodymyr Gavrish) plus DID_Wallet_metadata.csv

dataset_specification.description: 20,468 records, 117 features, imbalanced classes (27% class 1, 73% class 0); merged with dynamically generated identities and wallet addresses; evaluated under 10-fold nested cross-validation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalization, PCA dimensionality reduction, SMOTE oversampling, clustering with K-Means, feature construction from PCA components and temporal attributes, leak-free preprocessing fit on training folds only, calibration within training folds.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Nested stratified 10-fold cross-validation with 5 inner folds for tuning; 95% confidence intervals reported using DeLong for ROC-AUC and BCa bootstrap for BA/PR-AUC/Recall/F1.

implementation_details.framework_version: Qiskit (version not specified); Python 3.6; IBM Cloud Framework / watsonx.ai / Jupyter
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PCA, SMOTE, normalization, K-Means clustering, standardization, leak-free fold-wise fitting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Probability calibration (Platt/Isotonic), thresholding at 0.75, on-chain logging of state-check/score/decision
implementation_details.total_execution_time: ~45 s end-to-end runtime reported for the distributed pipeline

speedup_claims.conditions: end-to-end runtime comparison in the reported distributed pipeline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states QuanFraud runtime is about 45 s versus about 120 s for Maheshwari et al.; this is a system-level runtime comparison, not a pure quantum-circuit speedup.
No quantum advantage or asymptotic speedup claim is made; the paper explicitly emphasizes assurance-first trade-offs over accuracy or speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(nd) for the variational circuit depth d; GHZ preparation O(n) gates/qubits; QSVC/VQC polynomial in n and d
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: PCA O(nm^2) time and O(nm)+O(m^2) space; classical SVM O(n^2) mentioned for comparison

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 4 logical qubits for QSVC/VQC plus classical preprocessing; no demonstrated quantum advantage resources are identified.
limiting_factors: Classical baselines Random Forest and XGBoost achieve balanced accuracy above 77%, while QSVC is reported at 42.1 ± 2.8%
No quantum advantage claim is made
Only a 4-qubit simulator-based NISQ experiment is reported

experiments.description: GHZ-θ quantum state verification experiment for 4-qubit entanglement checking on IBM Quantum/Qiskit simulator, including Hadamard + CNOT GHZ preparation and fidelity thresholding at F > 0.5.

algorithm.variant: GHZ state preparation and theta-protocol verification
algorithm.ansatz: Hadamard followed by cascaded CNOTs to prepare |GHZ4>, then theta-protocol measurement

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare 4-qubit GHZ state from |0000> using H on q1 and cascaded CNOTs; verify with theta-protocol.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Verify entanglement/channel integrity; accept if fidelity exceeds threshold.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Abort on disturbance; accept only if F > 0.5.

problem_instance.description: 4-party GHZ verification for IoT/quantum-blockchain channel integrity and provenance.

dataset_specification.description: Ideal |GHZ4> = (|0000> + |1111>)/sqrt(2), with validation outcomes reported in Table III and Fig. 3.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: State preparation and theta-protocol verification; no classical preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Measurement outcomes for valid vs not valid GHZ states; fidelity thresholding at 0.5.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n) gate preparation for GHZ state

key_results: GHZ verification accepts ideal states with probability one in the noiseless description.
Under device noise, the paper reports acceptance for F > 0.5.
Table III reports valid vs not valid measurement outcomes for 4-qubit GHZ states.
